body:
PR929 implements the mixed-root cyclic inverse with four grouped calls and one dirty length-L connector. This construction splits the inverse into its nonnegative and strictly negative Laurent parts, applies two additive stable filters, and needs no borrowed length-L data array. Both calls restore the source exactly, including arbitrary nonzero lowest working bits; reversing call order and signs restores the target exactly.

The grouped Bezout solve handles repeated roots without requiring separation within either pole group. Laurent projection bounds the two numerator norms. Polynomial, scalar, numerator, recurrence-window, matrix, gauge and numerator-window preparation have explicit rounding budgets. For the inherited prime-power hypotheses, the written argument gives working precision at most `max(p,w)+12r^3` and conservative word allowance `A=max(p,w)+2m+64r^3`.

The supplied-neighboring-cycle cost is `soft-O(rL(A+B_phi)+r^3 log L(A+log L)+r^4(A+log L))`, with separately charged `O(r^3(A+log L+log r))` clean scalar bits. This clean workspace can exceed a data array for short cycles. The package does not provide a bit-reversible compiler, arbitrary-stride tape routing, common-label/Clifford realization, scalar-space hosting or the full multiplication reduction. **No new kappa.**

Validation on the frozen package:

- Full macOS/Python 3.11 and Linux/Python 3.14 replays, with isolation, optimization and bytecode disabled; complete mathematical receipts match byte for byte.
- 140 bounded cases, 48 original-kernel cases from all ten pinned fixtures through radix 16, 16 actual uniform-budget executions and 12 additional edge cases. Original-kernel cases meet the 128-bit target with coefficient preparation charged.
- 2,322 integer budget checks, eight exact nonnegative polynomial identities, 3,005 width boundary checks, 18 additional rejection controls and three boundary/precision defect families.
- Eleven package-corruption rejections and a full read-only relocated replay on each platform. Linux also starts with the supplied source package read-only.
- All 19 retained source files match their pinned SHA256 and Git objects. Selected-record consistency and staged whitespace checks pass.

Run `python3 -I -O -B research/additive-cyclic-no-connector/verify.py` and `python3 -I -O -B research/additive-cyclic-no-connector/test_package.py`. The scoped workflow repeats the full suite on Python 3.11/3.14; hosted CI is separate from local evidence.

Only the two new research directories and their workflow are added. The package credits PR621/628/862/905/929 and classical partial fractions, Laurent/Wiener bounds, companion filtering and Bareiss elimination. Finite checks support the written all-length argument; neither independent human review nor proof-assistant verification is claimed.
title: Research: two additive cyclic inverse calls with no dirty connector (no new kappa)
